record.paper_title: Open Problems in Heavy Quarkonium Physics
record.original_question: Why do Tevatron measurements of high-transverse-momentum charmonium production fail to show the transverse polarization expected from standard NRQCD gluon-fragmentation dynamics? In the scenario described in the paper, large-pT production is dominated by a transversely polarized gluon fragmenting into a color-octet 3S1 heavy-quark pair, and standard NRQCD power counting predicts that this transverse polarization should survive into the observed S-wave quarkonium state. The open problem is whether the discrepancy is due to experimental uncertainty, alternative power counting, or higher-order effects that dilute the polarization.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the framework of non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization for inclusive heavy quarkonium hadroproduction, the production cross section for an S-wave charmonium H (e.g. J/ψ or ψ(2S)) is written as a sum over intermediate heavy quark–antiquark Fock states n = ^{2S+1}L_J^{[1,8]} of short-distance partonic coefficients times long-distance NRQCD matrix elements ⟨O^H[n]⟩, with a power counting in the heavy-quark velocity v. At transverse momenta p_T much larger than the quarkonium mass, the leading short-distance mechanism is gluon fragmentation into a color-octet ^3S_1 c c̄ pair, and the fragmenting gluon is, to leading order in α_s, almost on-shell and therefore transversely polarized. Within standard v-power counting, the heavy-quark spin symmetry of NRQCD then predicts that the produced S-wave charmonium should inherit a sizable transverse polarization at large p_T, quantified by the polar angular distribution coefficient α → +1 (where dN/dcosθ ∝ 1 + α cos^2 θ in a suitable reference frame) as p_T → ∞.

Hadron-collider measurements of prompt J/ψ and ψ(2S) polarization at large p_T do not show this strong transverse polarization; instead α is observed to be small, and in some cases slightly longitudinal.

Problem: Determine, within NRQCD factorization (or a controlled modification of its power counting), the mechanism that resolves this discrepancy. Concretely:
(i) compute the polarization α(p_T) of prompt J/ψ and ψ(2S) at large p_T including all contributions (color-singlet and color-octet ^1S_0^{[8]}, ^3S_1^{[8]}, ^3P_J^{[8]}) consistently to higher orders in α_s and v, including effects such as soft-gluon emission off the intermediate color-octet pair, feed-down from heavier charmonia, and possible alternative power countings;
(ii) decide whether the observed lack of transverse polarization can be reconciled with NRQCD predictions while simultaneously describing the measured unpolarized p_T spectra of these states with a single, universal set of long-distance matrix elements ⟨O^H[n]⟩.
artifact.status_search_result: As of 2024–2025, the charmonium polarization puzzle remains unresolved. Recent reviews and LHC measurements (CMS, LHCb, ALICE) continue to report tension between NRQCD predictions—both LO and NLO—and the observed small/longitudinal polarization of prompt J/ψ and ψ(2S) at large p_T. No single set of long-distance matrix elements has been shown to simultaneously describe cross sections and polarizations across experiments; modified NRQCD approaches incorporating soft-gluon effects are being explored but the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Charmonia production at the LHC: an overview of recent results using NRQCD and modified NRQCD models
status_evidence.snippet: Significant discrepancies remain in the description of the transverse momentum dependence of quarkonium polarization in J/ψ hadroproduction, with NRQCD at LO and NLO failing to reproduce observed polarization patterns.
status_evidence.claim: NRQCD predictions still disagree with measured polarization patterns of J/ψ at large p_T.

status_evidence.title: Experimental Review of the Quarkonium Physics at the LHC
status_evidence.snippet: LHC measurements reveal limited polarization effects, challenging leading-order NRQCD predictions.
status_evidence.claim: LHC data confirm absence of strong transverse polarization predicted by standard NRQCD.
